It's all about whether you're someone who is capable of moderation or not. If you can't just have one, then you shouldn't have any.

I once spoke with an older man in the pub after a stressful day at work. He said something to be that really changed my perspective. I'd said to him casually that I felt bad because I'd drunk 3 glasses of wine in an hour (so one bottle). I explained that I was having a really hard time at work because I was being bullied by my managers. He told me about his wife dying, he said if it wasn't for having that escape with alcohol, when he just needed to get out of his thoughts and feelings for a while, that he had no doubt he wouldn't be here today. He used drinking as a way for him to cope, definitely not the best method by any means, but it gave him time to adjust and come to terms with losing his partner in his own time and made him realise it's ok to fall apart sometimes.

So no, I don't think drinking alone is wrong. Sometimes you just need to go on a bit of a bender and forget about whatever it is that's making your life hell. It's knowing when to stop and face up to it that's the important part.
That is if you're disciplined. It could easily spiral into an alcohol dependency, which is a relationship you don't want to have with such a substance.

I was and still am suffering from depression, and I used alcohol as a way to cope. When I got back to my apartment, alone and saddened, I needed alcohol to be able to make it through the night. Eventually it got to the point where I felt like I needed it all the time to escape, and I knew that I had to drastically cut down. I try only to drink on Friday nights and on the early weekend now. To start with, I am completely against Post-Modern Discussion here (I don't mind it existing, in other places), since it detracts from the quality discussion we might otherwise be having here, and it's an all-round poor debating tactic (you've all read the sidebar, it's nothing new I think). The only problem I see lies with what the admins of voat have long been saying: That they are completely in favour of free speech. I know most of the DE tend to be in favour of this as well, yet it really wouldn't be hard to say that we're hypocritical, since we are obviously disallowing a certain method of discourse. I'd say that this isn't really banning the submission of these ideas per se, more banning a certain mode of discussion. Others who cannot be bothered to read or understand the linked post may not see it quite that way. Any thoughts on how to reconcile this?
Possible Future Issues with disallowing Post-Modern Discussion?

There are two major concerns with post-modern discourse, that have the same root cause.

The first is Entryism, or the introduction of orthogonal ideas/values to the core philosophy. In an NRX board, the topics of discussion should stay almost entirely on subject matters directly related to NRX. Post-modern discourse makes it more difficult to guard against entryism by its very nature: it has a strong emphasis on inclusion, collaboration, and not offending anyone. All of these are methods in which the core philosophy may be subverted; it becomes difficult to stay on topic when you have to reconcile a multitude of competing opinions, and gradually the movement slows down.

The second is Relativism, most significantly, moral relativism. In a post-modern setting, all voices are equal, all cultures are equal, et cetera ad nauseam. When you allow relativism to take over, you slowly lose your own metric for determination of very important things: merit, truth, morality, ethics. When an emphasis is placed on equality and sensitivity, this all goes out the window, and a dysgenic effect takes place, both in the group and those still loyal.

These two are related in that they arise from a fundamental flaw in post-modern discourse: that it relies on a Subjective interpretation of reality. Modern discourse attempts to be as Objective as possible, because that's how reality is actually constructed. This is an age-old debate that goes back to Plato and Aristotle (and I will be making a long post about soon). Those who think rationally favor the Truth over all else, but what is the truth? Unfortunately that has a rather tenuous definition nowadays, in that context is often ignored (think Modal logic). A statement may be true in the present moment's context, yet in a universal (objective) context, it isn't, and therefore cannot be considered a Truth. Modern discourse places an emphasis on discovering the Truth (as objectively as it can) through reasoning and dissection of the arguments made. Postmodern discourse places an emphasis on who the speaker of he argument is, and the general feelings of those in the discussion. That is why postmodern discussions become circular, because they are inherently not objective, but subjective.

If you want actual activity, or this sub to represent anything more than a tiny theoretical group then you have to allow for chaos and organic growth.

This applies for darkly enlightened ideologies too, with people's fantasies of trying to win the upper-middle classes. It won't work, since they both have so much at stake in the system, and are the truest believers.
